ai.mechanism: Evidence shows only that the full USDC balance (2,500,050.09391 USDC, ~$2,500,050) left 0x233ba52c...76c5 in a single transaction. The packet carries no caller role, no permission or ownership data, no function selector, no call trace and no protocol identification, so no specific exploit mechanism can be named.
ai.lossBearer: Unidentified: the loss falls on whoever owns or is beneficiary of 0x233ba52c52b50eaf4da0681ff163455368ea76c5. No protocol, depositor set or integrator exposure is shown in the packet.
ai.narrative: A contract at 0x233ba52c...76c5 was emptied of its entire USDC balance, about 2.5 million dollars, in one transaction. That is the whole of what the evidence says. There is no protocol name, no depositor or integrator exposure, and nothing about who called the contract or whether they were permitted to. A treasury sweep, a bridge settlement or a vault migration looks exactly like this on chain. Without a caller role, a function called, or a token-holder base that just lost claim on those funds, calling this an exploit would be guessing, and there is no shown exposure path to trade against.
